target.title: fix (Computer Use) Stabilize Codex Computer Use readiness
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex Computer Use readiness could go stale or look healthy when it was not actually usable. OpenClaw agents can run with isolated per-agent `CODEX_HOME` directories, so one agent could keep a stale cached Computer Use plugin after the desktop app updated. Status/setup also reported coarse plugin availability without separately proving installation, MCP exposure, and live `list_apps` behavior.

The macOS desktop bundle has also moved from `/Applications/Codex.app` to `/Applications/ChatGPT.app`. A managed integration that only probes the legacy bundle can lose both the app-server binary and bundled Computer Use marketplace after the desktop update.

## Summary

This PR hardens Codex Computer Use setup so OpenClaw no longer treats “plugin exists somewhere” as sufficient readiness.

It adds:

- shared local bundled Computer Use plugin cache reconciliation for per-agent `CODEX_HOME` directories, defaulting to a real copied cache entry that Codex can discover and removing stale cached versions
- current/legacy macOS desktop compatibility: managed app-server and bundled marketplace discovery prefer `ChatGPT.app`, fall back to `Codex.app`, then retain the existing plugin-local/package binary fallbacks
- decomposed `/codex computer-use status` results for installation, MCP exposure, and a live `computer-use.list_apps` probe
- truthful readiness: a failed live probe always reports `ready: false`; startup compatibility is evaluated separately when `strictReadiness` is false, while `strictReadiness: true` fails closed
- explicit `/codex computer-use install` remains strict and only succeeds after installation, MCP exposure, and the live probe all pass
- a 60s live-probe timeout, exactly one 60s retry, and opt-in narrow auto-repair that only terminates stale `SkyComputerUseClient ... mcp` children when `computerUse.autoRepair` is true
- opt-in periodic per-shared-client Computer Use health probes when `computerUse.healthCheckEnabled` is true, using the configured 30/60/120/240 minute cadence and the same live-probe path
- config/schema/docs for `liveTestTimeoutMs`, `toolCallTimeoutMs`, `leaseTimeoutMs`, `healthCheckEnabled`, `healthCheckIntervalMinutes`, `pluginCacheMode`, `strictReadiness`, and `autoRepair`
- a window-scope Computer Use lease manager with renewal/preemption semantics for callers that can supply a stable window id
- `openclaw doctor` surfacing for enabled Codex Computer Use, including configured health cadence and the status command to inspect installation/exposure/live-test layers

## Context

This addresses the failure mode where one OpenClaw agent could keep using a stale per-agent Codex plugin cache after the desktop app had a newer bundled Computer Use plugin, and where status/setup could report only coarse plugin availability instead of separating install state, MCP exposure, and live runtime health.

The previous direction in #96730 improved app-server command selection/startup behavior, but it did not make Computer Use readiness globally inspectable across agents, reconcile isolated per-agent plugin caches with the locally installed desktop bundle, or prove the MCP bridge with a real `list_apps` call before reporting readiness. This PR closes those gaps locally and offline; it does not depend on a remote marketplace.

## Notes

The new lease manager is window-scoped by design, not app-scoped and not host-global. Native Codex MCP notifications are observational, so full pre-execution enforcement requires Computer Use tool payloads to expose a stable window identifier before the MCP call begins. The PR documents that boundary and adds the tested lease primitive for call sites that can provide that scope.

For local marketplace installation, Codex expects the marketplace **root directory** as the `marketplace/add` source. The individual Computer Use `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` is a plugin descriptor, not a marketplace source. After registration, Codex returns the marketplace manifest path and OpenClaw uses that manifest path plus `pluginName: "computer-use"` for `plugin/read` and `plugin/install`.

## Evidence

Exact head: `1457beece174132276fef1a386f256b2f6270ebd`, rebased on `origin/main` `47ec6237ffbc28b9fa711799357d9745f47ad6ab`.

Exact-head verification:

- 10 focused Codex test files / 346 tests passed, covering startup, managed binary resolution, config, cache reconciliation, health, leases, Computer Use setup/live probing, request guards, shared clients, and commands
- Codex extension production and test typechecks passed
- Codex extension lint passed: 0 warnings / 0 errors across 6,328 files
- touched-file `oxfmt --check` passed
- docs formatting, MDX validation, docs-map validation, markdownlint, and `git diff --check` passed

Current ChatGPT desktop live proof, executed through the exact PR head in a temporary isolated `CODEX_HOME`:

- selected managed command: `/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex`
- app-server version: `0.144.0-alpha.4`
- selected bundled marketplace root: `/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/plugins/openai-bundled`
- returned marketplace manifest: `/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/plugins/openai-bundled/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`
- installation ready: true
- plugin installed/enabled: true/true
- MCP exposure: 10 tools
- live `list_apps` probe: passed on the first attempt

Live marketplace-source semantics were also checked with isolated Codex homes:

- the ChatGPT bundled marketplace root directory is accepted by `codex plugin marketplace add`
- the marketplace JSON file is rejected as an add source because it is a file
- the individual Computer Use `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` is rejected for the same reason

Compatibility coverage proves:

- `ChatGPT.app` is preferred when both desktop bundle candidates exist
- legacy `Codex.app` is selected when `ChatGPT.app` is absent
- plugin-local/package managed binary fallback remains intact
- bundled marketplace auto-registration and shared-cache reconciliation use the same current-then-legacy precedence
- explicit app-server command and marketplace overrides remain authoritative
- explicit marketplace cache namespaces are preserved by shared-cache reconciliation
- the direct MCP probe sandbox bypass remains constrained to the configured Computer Use server's `list_apps` call
